name: Huppim
title: Benjamin's descendant
summary: Huppim was a son (or descendant) of Benjamin, Jacob's youngest son with Rachel. He is mentioned in the genealogies in Genesis and 1 Chronicles as part of Benjamin's lineage. His significance lies primarily in his place in Israel's tribal history as part of the tribe of Benjamin.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned among the sons of Benjamin
keyEvents.description: Huppim is listed as one of Benjamin's sons in the genealogy of Jacob's family that went down to Egypt.

keyEvents.title: Jacob's Family Goes to Egypt
keyEvents.description: As part of Jacob's extended family, Huppim was among the seventy people who traveled to Egypt during the famine, where Joseph served as second-in-command.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the Genealogies of Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Huppim is mentioned again in 1 Chronicles in connection with Benjamin's genealogy, where the descendants of the tribe are recorded.

keyEvents.title: The Inheritance of the Tribe of Benjamin
keyEvents.description: As a patriarch within Benjamin's lineage, Huppim contributed to the continued existence of this tribe, which later produced Israel's first king, Saul.
